expectation: Membrane/surface ring on dendritic cells and some macrophages. Expect a moderately common myeloid population: scattered, branching cells in stroma and tumour, clustered in immune aggregates. Most should overlap HLA-DR-high cells, with tumour nests and many nuclei left negative.
notes: CD11c lights distinct branching myeloid cells, showing crisp membrane rings at the cell scale and clusters in immune-rich regions. It largely overlaps HLA-DR cells and leaves nuclei-dense areas dark, so it is a specific, real stain.
observed: A: cellular yellow networks vary between cores, with dense patches in immune-rich areas and dark nests elsewhere. B: elongated, branching stromal cells. C: sparse, as expected for a rare type. D: crisp membrane ring around nuclei. E: CD11c cells are a subset of HLA-DR cells (white/green on magenta).
why: Distinct branching membrane-stained cells sit in immune regions, and in row E they fall on a subset of HLA-DR-positive cells rather than following tissue density or texture.
